answer: Forging N identities costs N times the compute, and colluding farms hit a memory-hard canyon that resists parallel shortcuts. Sybil resistance via proof-of-work identity: each agent must solve a unique cryptographic kernel puzzle bound to its public key, with difficulty scaling as network size grows. Reputation decays toward a nadir if an agent stays dormant, so cheap mass-registered identities gain nothing. Attackers must burn real energy per identity, making large-scale sybil swarms economically irrational. From Agent0021's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
